Sam / Hannah — did a quick technical pass and high-level math below. These are conservative, intentionally rounded numbers for planning; we can refine on the call.

Assumptions:
- Orion-XL-32k weights (FP16) ~= 140 GB.
- Quantized (4-bit, Q4) weights ~= 36–42 GB depending on quantizer and per-layer fallback.
- Active workspace (activations, attention buffers, temp) ~= 6–12 GB depending on runtime and batch size.
- KV cache per active session at 32k context: estimate ~180–260 MB/session (depends on hidden size and layer count). We use 220 MB as a mid estimate.

Per-replica GPU memory snapshot (approx):
- FP16 replica: weights 140 GB -> requires multi-GPU split or weight-offload (not hostable on single 80GB). Practical hosting options: model sharding across 2x80GB GPUs (with NCCL) or larger 160+GB GPU nodes. Runtime mem + KV (per session) additive.
- Q4 replica: weights ~40 GB + workspace 10 GB + 2–4 GB for runtime overhead = ~56 GB baseline. Add KV per session (0.22 GB). So a single A100-80GB can host 1 Q4 replica with headroom for a few concurrent sessions if using batching and sharing KV? For dedicated serving, you should count per-concurrency KV*concurrency when sessions cannot share cache.

Sizing guidance for your profile (15 steady / 50 peak):
Option A — conservative, lower risk (favor minimal latency spikes):
- Provision 6 x 80GB GPUs as Q4 replicas (each replica serves ~6–8 concurrent sessions with our runtime + batching), working set supports ~48 steady concurrency headroom (6 * 8) and absorbs bursts to 50 with autoscale buffer. This assumes effective prefix caching and some request coalescing.

Option B — aggressive cost-optimized (more quant + routing):
- Use 4 x 80GB Q4 replicas for the bulk of traffic (serves ~32 steady concurrent). Route heavier context (>=20k tokens) to Q4 replicas and shorter sessions (<=8k) to a 13B Q4 fleet (can be hosted at 2–3 replicas per 80GB). Combine with autoscaling for peak-to-peak. Expect ~20–30% lower committed spend but added routing complexity + small quality delta on some prompts.

Quantization tradeoffs:
- Q4 gives the biggest win for memory and usually enables single-replica on 80GB GPUs. Perf-wise, Q4 adds modest CPU/GPU kernel overhead; throughput per GPU is often similar or slightly lower than FP16. Q2 or extreme quant reduces memory more but risks quality regressions on open weights and reduces throughput predictability.

Operational notes:
- KV cache at 32k context is meaningful — treat it like per-session RAM; if you have many long-lived sessions, that adds up. Consider session eviction policies and prefix caching.
- Recommend reserving an extra 1–2 GPUs (20–30% buffer) for rollout/canary and model upgrades.
- If you require single-node hosting for simplicity, you will need 2 x 80GB GPUs per FP16 replica (or larger 160+GB HW).

Estimated committed pool recommendation (first pass):
- Base plan (balanced): 6 x A100-80GB, Q4 runtime, standard autoscale allowance for spikes.
- Cost-optimized hybrid: 4 x A100-80GB (Orion Q4) + 3 x A100-80GB hosting 13B routing variants + autoscale.

I'll bring a small slide with these numbers to the call. If you want, I can also produce a per-hour token cost estimate and a simple price model for committed vs burst usage.

-Marcus
